rocket-moon:
Use case: illustration-story. Create a polished children's picture book illustration atlas for "Rocket to the Moon". It is a production game texture: a tall portrait canvas divided into EXACTLY 2 COLUMNS and 4 ROWS, eight equally sized rectangular panels, reading left-to-right then top-to-bottom. Every panel must remain exactly in its own grid cell with no overlap; no panel outlines, no gutters, no titles, no text, no letters, no numbers. Each panel has a complete illustrated background. Soft hand-painted children's storybook gouache and watercolor with readable dark contours, colorful and beautiful, appealing to young children. Keep the same characters, clothes, objects and colour palette consistent across all eight panels. Gentle expressions and warm lighting, imaginative detailed environments, not clipart. Do not use copyrighted characters. Scenes in order:
Panel 1: Child Ari with curly dark hair in white teal spacesuit, small round orange robot Pip, red white rocket, starry launch pad.
Panel 2: Same rocket lifts gently from launch pad with soft orange plume; Ari and Pip visible in round window.
Panel 3: Ari and orange robot look through rocket window at blue white Earth, dark space.
Panel 4: Rocket landed on grey moon; child in sealed helmet and small robot step down ladder, Earth distant.
Panel 5: Child in sealed spacesuit makes small playful hop on moon, robot and footprints, rocket nearby.
Panel 6: Ari and robot observe rounded crater from safe flat edge, sketch pad, rocket in distance.
Panel 7: Child and orange robot inside warm rocket cabin press blue radio button, moon visible through window.
Panel 8: Ari without spacesuit and small orange toy robot on garden picnic blanket, cardboard rocket, moon overhead.
The grid is critical: 2 equal-width columns, 4 equal-height rows. Fill the canvas edge-to-edge with the 8 separate panels. Portrait aspect ratio approximately 2:3.

dinosaurs: Edit target: supplied dinosaur atlas. Fix production sprite clipping. Keep atlas landscape 1536x1024, exactly 3 columns and 2 rows, cells 512x512. Each complete animal must fit inside the central 300x300 pixels of its cell, leaving at least 100 pixels of fully transparent clearance from EVERY cell boundary. Preserve complete tails/wings and species-specific anatomy. Remove all background glows/shadows/color clouds: background alpha zero. No labels, no drawn boxes, no scenery.
